limitations: Tier 2 (v5 domains) and Tier 3 (crucible.civ) do not exist in this checkout: S.2, S.3, S.5, SP-11.1, OO.1, OO.3, OO.4, OO.5, OO.6 fail with tiers_covered/tiers_supported = 1 and say why; their adapters are written (Tier 2 against domains.base, unit-tested with a test-module domain; Tier 3 against the specified civ entry point).

A raw World.create without the spec param evaluator_access keeps the 4.0 contract (4.0 families, scripted agents and logs unchanged); only learner-facing constructors build observation-only worlds. Adopting an existing World (KernelExperienceEnv(World), the AGENTRS adapters, Gym/PZ with world_id, MCP handlers, WorldEnv from a snapshot) sets the policy as a runtime override, which a regenerated copy of that world does not carry.

Field filtering applies to participants acting through tools, results and events (and nested calls a participant started). In-world simulated participants driven by module processes (innovation adopters, population) still read some evaluator data through module internals (workstreams G/B, D-18); innovation adopters write their hidden-truth score into free-text adoption notes (innovation/adopt.py) that providers see - free text written by simulated participants is not filtered.

The evaluator-only status of tools, fields and metrics is a curated registry (core/evaluator_only.py) plus the endpoint flag; the probes cover the worlds and tools exercised (a sweep over every read-only tool of a kernel world with v5 modules), not every module of every family.
Learners in the same process can always read env.world; isolation from the verifier is real only through crucible.experience.host (a separate process).

The self-play harness outside legacy mode computes an individual's own signal from its observation (revenue minus cost) and refuses joint/mixed/score objectives; the self-play learners themselves (climber reads the reward slot) are workstream K's to redesign. Research protocols take reward_mode but their positive controls still read the environment reward (workstream N).
Tier 1 rapid tick duration is DEFAULT_TICK_S = 3600 s unless a family defines tick_s; the rapid adapter reads RapidEnv._events/_state/_ledger (no public indexed event API yet).
Kernel and mechanism execute results carry no monetary cost field (CAM ExecutionResult.cost); rapid results carry cost_cents.
OO.5 limits are the run's own (memory growth, wall time, in-memory event log); a store-backed world is needed for runs far beyond 90 days.
